title: SubagentTool pipeline

findings.title: Malformed batch_tasks entries silently dropped; all-malformed array collapses the fan-out into a single run
findings.summary: filter_map drops any batch entry that is not an object with a non-empty string 'task' (e.g. an array of strings). Partial drops renumber results with no notice; when every entry is malformed has_batch=false and the call silently runs the top-level task as one ordinary sub-agent, reported as success.
findings.impact: Model believes an N-way fan-out ran when it did not; results indices shift; no diagnostic anywhere in the response.
findings.fix: Fail the parse with a per-index message instead of filter_map; also error when batch_tasks is present but not an array.

findings.title: Wrong-typed scalars silently coerced to defaults while unknown keys are rejected loudly
findings.summary: timeout_secs (as_u64, :133/:240), run_in_background (as_bool, :246), synthesize (as_bool, :297) and the array fields fall back to defaults on a type mismatch. "run_in_background": "true" blocks the parent turn synchronously; "timeout_secs": 300.0 silently becomes 120.
findings.impact: Same 'ran with a different meaning than asked, reported success' failure reject_unknown_keys exists to prevent, one level down.
findings.fix: Distinguish absent/null from present-with-wrong-type; return a typed error per field via small req_bool/req_u64/req_array helpers.

findings.title: MoA aggregator prompt concatenates every proposal in full, unbounded
findings.summary: build_synthesis_prompt appends each proposal's entire final_text with no per-proposal or total cap; record_batch_row clones the full text into proposals. Child output is unbounded.
findings.impact: Wide fan-outs of verbose children produce an oversized aggregator prompt -> prompt_too_long / provider error after the whole fan-out has already been paid for. Only unbounded accumulation in an otherwise carefully bounded pipeline.
findings.fix: Char-wise cap per proposal and on the assembled prompt, with an explicit truncation marker (no silent caps).

findings.title: Sub-agent output interpolated into the aggregator prompt with markdown delimiters and no fencing (prompt injection)
findings.summary: Proposal bodies (which routinely embed external untrusted tool/web/file content) are concatenated between '### Proposal N' headings and a trailing '## Your task' instruction with no escaping or external-content fence.
findings.impact: A proposal can forge the frame: re-open the instruction section, impersonate another proposer, or steer the aggregator whose answer the parent consumes as the batch result.
findings.fix: Fence each proposal with the repo's external-content boundary (content_sanitizer::split_external_fence) or an escaped XML tag, and rewrite interior markers via tool_output/fence.rs::rewrite_interior.

findings.title: A child queued on the concurrency semaphore is invisible to its own timeout_secs on the foreground and aggregator paths
findings.summary: subagent_spawner::spawn acquires the permit before arming tokio::time::timeout. The sync batch compensates with fanout_deadline and documents exactly this; the foreground single run (:1297-1317) and the MoA aggregator (:1144-1147) await the runtime directly with no queue-aware backstop.
findings.impact: With the default cap of 4 and four background children of the same session holding permits, a run with timeout_secs=120 can block the parent turn until the 1_800_000 ms tool budget fires (~30 min). The schema advertises timeout_secs as the maximum the sub-agent may run.
findings.fix: Wrap both awaits in timeout_at, or move the queue wait inside the spawner's own clock so 'Sub-agent timed out after Ns' covers queueing (single source; lets the batch drop its separate backstop).

findings.title: execute is a ~1190-line function in a 1902-line file
findings.summary: async fn execute spans :158-:1349 with up to six nesting levels, mixing seven actions, the batch fan-out state machine, the deadline/grace/abort drain and the MoA reduce; the default-agent resolution is duplicated three times inside it.
findings.impact: Exceeds the repo's 500-line split threshold (P2 / CODE_ORGANIZATION.md); invariants like the deadline-snapshotted 'incomplete' require ~200 lines of context to verify.
findings.fix: Extract per-action handlers and split the run path into run_batch_sync / run_batch_background / run_single / run_moa_reduce; execute becomes a dispatch table.

findings.title: Sync-batch legs re-establish three of the four carried task-locals; background path uses CarriedAttribution (four)
findings.summary: spawn.rs uses CarriedAttribution (scope, project_root, agent_id, CALLER_ROLE); the batch legs hand-roll only the first three, and the file's own source guard (REQUIRED_TASK_LOCALS, :1827) encodes that same three-item list so it cannot see the omission.
findings.impact: Latent, not live: run_agent_loop does not re-establish CALLER_ROLE either, so both paths capture None today and tool gating flows through TurnContext.caller_role. The defect is the duplicated ritual CarriedAttribution exists to prevent; an absent role is fail-OPEN if it ever becomes live.
findings.fix: Use CarriedAttribution::capture()/reestablish() in the batch legs and retarget the source guard at those two symbols instead of a literal list of three combinators.

findings.title: The 'default' agent fallback bypasses the resolve_spawnable predicate (3 sites)
findings.summary: Explicit agent_type goes through resolve_spawnable (mode == SubAgent filter, added to close the 'agent_type = main -> Primary wildcard grant' hole). The fallbacks at :788, :1085 and :1245 call lookup_with_overlay("default") with no mode filter.
findings.impact: Not currently exploitable (builtin/loader/plugin defaults are all SubAgent), but AgentRegistry::register accepts any AgentDef, so one Primary-mode 'default' registration re-opens the hole on the path taken whenever the model omits agent_type.
findings.fix: Call resolve_spawnable("default", project_root_ref) at all three sites, keeping the existing miss arm.

findings.title: enumerate is order-dependent while its sibling classify is explicitly order-independent
findings.summary: classify returns early on SubagentReturned ('Returned beats Spawned regardless of order'); enumerate's doc claims a Returned 'upgrades' the Spawned entry but the code is a blind last-write-wins insert, so a Spawned record after its Returned downgrades Completed to Interrupted. SessionService::get_events documents no ordering guarantee.
findings.impact: list would label a finished child 'interrupted ... it never finished', inviting the model to redo completed work — the exact failure the module exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Make Completed absorbing in the merge (entry().and_modify(...).or_insert(...)) so both readers share one precedence rule.

verified_clean: All 29 SubagentTool fields are populated at the construction site (run_loop/inner.rs:990-1195) and threaded into every child runtime by build_runtime (spawn.rs:353-423); all three spawn paths share it, so there is no per-path drift.

subagent_semaphore_for (types.rs:68-85) performs get/retain/insert under one held Mutex guard — no double-init race; with_parent_session_id's semaphore rebind happens during construction before any Arc clone escapes.

Every spawn/await site derives its token through cancel_for_child_with and pairs it with a CancelGuard or explicit .cancel(); act.rs never cancels the per-call child token on normal completion, so background children correctly outlive a finished parent turn.

The 'Sub-agent timed out' prefix predicate is byte-identical across producer (subagent_spawner:668) and both consumers (runtime.rs:426, background_tracker.rs:98); cancel classification uses exact equality.
No cross-session disclosure reachable via the by-id faces: progress_snapshot takes no scope but every caller is gated first, and wait_any classifies out-of-scope ids as NotFound rather than TimedOut.
